name: Kok-Jaiyk Valley
full: Kok-Jaiyk Valley (“Valley of Flowers”, Kok-Jaiyk jailoo (summer pasture) in the Jeti-Oguz gorge)
near: The Jeti-Oguz resort (a sanatorium, ≈4 km in a straight line, 6–8 km by road up the gorge); the village of Jeti-Oguz is at the mouth of the gorge; Karakol is 25–28 km away.
elev: ≈2,300 m at the Kok Zhaiyk Yurt Camp (Destination Jeti-Oguz); Nomad's Land gives 2,540 m for the meadows higher up; the valley rises from ≈2,200 m (the sanatorium) to ≈2,600 m.
short: A wide high-mountain meadow at the head of the Jeti-Oguz gorge above the red “Seven Bulls” cliffs: summer pastures with yurts, flowering meadows in June, birch and spruce groves, and the “Girl’s Braids” waterfall (≈40 m) in a side gorge. Accessible by car (6–8 km of dirt road with bridges) or on foot in 3 h from the resort.
desc: Kok-Jaiyk (“green meadow”, which tourists call the “Valley of Flowers”) begins where the narrow Jeti-Oguz gorge, after the fifth wooden bridge, suddenly opens into a spacious valley with boulders, hayfields and yurts on the slopes. It is one of the main summer pastures of the southern shore: in May–June the meadows are covered with flowers, and in winter with snow. From the Jeti-Oguz resort (with its hydrogen sulfide springs at 2,200 m) 6–8 km of bumpy dirt road with five bridges over the river lead here — an SUV can drive it, and in summer ordinary cars can too at low speed; the entrance to the gorge is paid, through a barrier of the Jeti-Oguz forestry enterprise. In the valley there are family yurt camps with meals and horses; from them trails start to the “Girl’s Braids” waterfall (Maiden’s Tears; ≈300 m through spruce forest from the upper yurts, and according to reviews the trail disappears among the branches) and farther on — to Oguz-Bashi Peak (5,181 m), to Teleti and to Lake Ala-Kul. Above the valley there are views of the snow-capped peaks of the Terskey Ala-Too.
guide: Go in June: Kok-Jaiyk is not called the “Valley of Flowers” for nothing — the slopes are then blue and yellow with lupine and buttercups, and by August they are mown. Count the bridges: after the fifth the road comes out onto the meadow — stop there, because farther on cars only get in the way. To the “Girl’s Braids” waterfall go from the yurts along the path through the spruce forest, without turning onto the livestock tracks — travelers regularly add an extra 1.5 km; it is easier with a horse and a local guide. Ask your yurt hosts for kumis and flatbreads, not just a photo with a golden eagle: shepherds still live here, it is not only an “attraction”. If you want more, a trek starts here through Teleti to Ala-Kul and the Karakol gorge, 2–3 days.
see: The meadow with yurts and boulders; flowering meadows (May–June); the “Girl’s Braids” waterfall (~40 m); birch and spruce groves; views of Oguz-Bashi (5,181 m); on the way — the red “Seven Bulls” and “Broken Heart” cliffs; the Jeti-Oguz sanatorium with hot springs.
skip: If you have already seen the Seven Bulls and do not have 2–3 hours for the dirt road and a walk — the meadow is beautiful, but it is “one more jailoo”. If you go in August after the haymaking and expect a “valley of flowers” — the flowers are gone. If you are in a low-clearance car after rain — the bridges and ruts will be a problem.
diff: Easy for the drive and a stroll on the meadow; to the waterfall — a short but choppy climb through the forest (30–60 min); on foot from the resort — 3 h, 6–8 km, gain ≈300–400 m. Further treks — moderate/high.
when: Late May–June (flowering), July–August (yurts, the season), September (gold, few people). In winter the valley is accessible with snow, the yurts do not operate (Nomad's Land: year-round). In spring after the thaw — mud and high water at the bridges.
hours: Open 24 hours; the forestry barrier at the gorge entrance — paid passage in the daytime in season (Kaktus, 06.2025); the yurt camps — roughly June–September.
daytime: Morning (leave Karakol at 8:00–9:00 per Destination Karakol’s recommendation) — light on the red cliffs on the way and coolness on the climb to the waterfall; return by 16:00 on a marshrutka (minibus) from the resort.
how: From Karakol: marshrutka No. 372 or a shared taxi from the Ak-Tilek bazaar to the Jeti-Oguz resort — 100 som/person (in summer some trips may end in the village — ask for “Jeti-Oguz kurort”); a taxi ≈1,800 som per car one way (Destination Karakol). From the resort — 6–8 km up the gorge by car (5 bridges) or 3 h on foot. From Bishkek — ≈5 h by car to Jeti-Oguz.
needcar: Not necessarily: a marshrutka to the resort + 3 h on foot. By car an SUV/crossover is advisable (bumps, bridges); in summer in dry weather ordinary cars get through.
self: Yes: the road is obvious (up the gorge across the bridges), the meadow is open; for the waterfall it is better to ask the yurt hosts for directions or take a guide.
roadtype: Karakol → resort — paved; above the resort 6–8 km of dirt road with bumps, climbs and five wooden bridges (ZigZag on Earth; varandej); in 2018 — 7 km of gravel to the yurts (frantsouzov). Passable for an SUV; after rain — only 4×4. Inside the valley — trails.
traveltime: Karakol → Jeti-Oguz resort 30–40 min; resort → meadow 20–30 min by car or ≈3 h on foot; meadow → waterfall 30–60 min on foot. A full day from Karakol — 8–9 h with lunch.
stay: Kok Zhaiyk Yurt Camp (Destination Jeti-Oguz, jetioguz.travel) — yurts at 2,300 m, national cuisine, horseback outings; prices on request via a form. Family yurt camps in the valley — through CBT Karakol (ZigZag on Earth: mattresses, Western toilets, a shower in one of the camps). The Jeti-Oguz sanatorium below. 2026 prices are not published.
net: Beeline strengthened its network in Jeti-Oguz in April 2026 (economist.kg) — there is a signal at the village and the resort; in the Kok-Jaiyk valley beyond the bridges the reception is weak/absent according to reports, there are no measurements. Offline map.
entry: Passage through the barrier of the Jeti-Oguz forestry enterprise (Kaktus.media, 10.06.2025): car 50–80 som, large vehicles 100–250, buses 200–300 som per entry; pedestrians in Jeti-Oguz do not pay (the fee is charged only on vehicles). Earlier (2018) ≈200 rubles were charged per car. The waterfall and the meadow — no separate fee.
transfer: Marshrutka 100 som/person; taxi 1,800 som per car one way (Destination Karakol); MYWAY 8,000 som round trip with waiting (2026); a Tripster excursion €240 per group (2026).
bring: Shoes for forest and rocks, a windbreaker/fleece (it is cool at 2,300–2,500 m), a rain jacket, cash som (barrier, yurts, horses), water, repellent, sun protection.
warn:
Since 21.07.2025 there has been an eco-post at the Kok-Jaiyk entrance: private cars are not allowed onto the pasture (24.kg). Go up on foot, on horseback or by permitted transport.

Do not swim in the river — icy water and a strong current; do not approach horses and cows from behind (ZigZag). The trail to the waterfall disappears in the spruce forest — it is easy to wander onto livestock tracks. The bridges are wooden — check their condition after a flood. Drones lose their compass in the narrow gorge (2018 report). The entry is paid through the forestry enterprise, demand a receipt.
food: In the valley’s yurts: kumis, kaymak and flatbreads, lagman, manti, soups, pancakes (ZigZag); lunch in a yurt is included in the Tripster excursions. At the Jeti-Oguz resort — the sanatorium canteen; in Karakol — ashlyan-fu and Dungan cuisine.
reviews: The site has no Google listing (ambiguous result). According to reports from 2013–2026 (varandej, frantsouzov, ZigZag on Earth, 24.kg readers, a Tripster organizer 4.9): pros — space, flowers, yurts with living everyday life, the waterfall; cons — the bumpy road, the trail to the waterfall that gets lost, and in summer many local picnickers.
p.sum: Kok-Jaiyk is a meadow valley above the Jeti-Oguz resort, 25–28 km from Karakol. From Karakol: marshrutka No. 355/372 to the resort (≈100 som) or a taxi (1,000–1,800 som one way), then 6–8 km of dirt road with five wooden bridges — by crossover/jeep (after rain only 4×4) or 2.5–3 h on foot. It is worth staying overnight in a yurt camp at 2,300 m (from $13 at Kok Zhaiyk Yurt Camp to $50 with breakfast at Ecotrek), and in the morning going to the waterfall (2.5 km, +161 m) and riding across the meadows. Vehicle entry through the forestry barrier is paid (50–80 som), pedestrians do not pay.

p.iti.1.title: 2 days
p.iti.1.plan: Day 1: Karakol → Jeti-Oguz, climb on foot 3 h, a night in a yurt. Day 2: in the morning ride across the meadows 2–3 h, the waterfall, descent; on the way — Barskoon or Skazka along the southern shore.
p.iti.2.title: What to combine it with
p.iti.2.plan: The Jeti-Oguz gorge, the Maiden’s Tears waterfall, the Chon-Kyzyl-Suu gorge (the next one to the west), Karakol; then the southern shore — Barskoon, Skazka.
p.season: Late May–June: flowering (“Valley of Flowers”); July–August: yurts, peak; September — gold, few people; October — frosts; winter — snow, Ecotrek operates (skis, snowshoes); spring — mud, high water.
p.budget.economy: ≈2,000–3,500 som for 2 days: marshrutka 100×2, yurt ≈700–1,100 ($13), food 600–1,000, horse 800
p.budget.comfort: ≈10,000–15,000 som/person: MYWAY transfer 8,000 or Ecotrek $70 per car, Ecotrek $50 + meals $30, a guided horseback ride
p.permits: Not needed. The barrier of the Jeti-Oguz forestry enterprise charges only vehicles (car 50–80 som, 2025); pedestrians free; the waterfall — free.
p.access: With children — excellent (meadows, a short trail to the waterfall); for older people — by jeep to the yurts; with a stroller — no; with a dog — possible (livestock, shepherd dogs).
